title: Democrats Need to Talk About Immigration
summary: Radical right-wing parties have advanced across Western countries by successfully tying immigration to voters’ diffuse fears about their economic well-being, personal security, and cultural identity. Rather than ignoring or co-opting such claims, mainstream parties must offer equally robust counternarratives.

title: War in an Age of Weak Powers
summary: The war in Iran has weakened both the United States and China, exposing the limits of their military power and strategic influence. Their troubles are creating a more dangerous geopolitical landscape while providing Europe with a rare opportunity to reform its governance model and reinvent its global role.

title: Hedging the AI Doomsday Risk
summary: As far-fetched as warnings of an impending AI apocalypse may sound, even a remote risk should not be dismissed outright when human extinction is at stake. To guard against a danger of such extraordinary scale, governments and companies need to go beyond conventional risk-management strategies.

title: AI Is Only as Trustworthy as the Internet
summary: Trust in technology is eroding at the very moment AI is putting more power in the hands of governments and Big Tech. Rebuilding that trust requires keeping the internet open and accessible so that new technologies can develop through broad participation rather than being shaped by the interests of a powerful few.

title: AI Demands Simpler Financial Regulation
summary: AI could undermine financial oversight by giving market participants new ways to circumvent rules that regulators never anticipated. Overly complicated regulations give AI agents more ways to game the system, underscoring the need to streamline existing frameworks and equip officials with AI tools of their own.
